newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan economy still in moderate recovery trend-BOJ.
newsitem.headline: Japan economy still in moderate recovery trend-BOJ.

text.p: Japan's economy is continuing on a moderate recovery trend supported by the yen's depreciation until early spring and the expansion of information-related demand, the Bank of Japan (BOJ) said in its quarterly economic outlook released on Thursday.
But the central bank also said the recovery was unlikely to gather significant momentum in view of fragility in some sectors as well as continued pressure from balance-sheet adjustments.

The BOJ report said that despite restraining pressures from fiscal policy, including a rise in the sales tax on April 1 and a decline in public-sector investment, the economy was expected to continue its recovery.
It said net exports had recently increased significantly, and were likely to continue to be steady. Capital spending had also been rising steadily and could be expected to continue increasing.
However, capital spending was unlikely to gather significant momentum for the time being due to an absence of rapidly expanding industries and remaining balance-sheet adjustment pressures.

The report said that the recovery trend in personal consumption did not seem to have been hindered despite a fall off in consumer demand after the sales tax rise. It said industrial production had been firm and that the growth in employees' incomes had been rising steadily, albeit moderately.
The report also said that prices had been stable, although indices were pushed up by the consumption tax increase.

It said that developments in commercial land prices had varied. Prices of land near city centres and of that suitable for major development had more or less stopped declining, but prices of irregular-shaped small plots had continued to decline.
He added that prices of residential land had virtually stopped declining, particularly in Tokyo.

The report also said that market expectations for higher interest rates were not as strong as before, citing a moderation in the slope in the euroyen futures curve after it had become steep at the end of May.

It said the long-term government bond yield had risen to near 2.7 percent in late May, but had fallen after the market reconfirmed the moderate pace of the economic recovery and had recently been moving at around 2.2-2.3 percent.
The report said that the market had become somewhat cautious about the Japan's economic outlook and interest rates for the next three years or so.
